medications.duration: Lifelong – review annually and titrate as tolerated
medications.purpose: Renin‑angiotensin system blockade to reduce proteinuria and slow CKD progression
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ACE‑I for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension; monitor creatinine and potassium after 1‑2 weeks

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a CV‑risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 advises statin for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

medications.duration: Lifelong – review annually; start only if BP remains >130/80 mmHg after ACE‑I titration
medications.purpose: Additional blood pressure control to achieve target <130/80 mmHg in proteinuric CKD
medications.nice_justification: NG203 BP target <130/80 mmHg when ACR ≥70 mg/mmol; CCB is recommended adjunct after ACE‑I

medications.dose: 5,000 IU subcutaneously weekly (adjust to Hb response)
medications.purpose: Treat anemia of chronic kidney disease
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ESA after iron repletion for symptomatic CKD‑related anemia

medications.purpose: Correct vitamin D deficiency and manage CKD‑MBD
medications.nice_justification: NG203 advises vitamin D supplementation for bone health in CKD

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive antihypertensive effect may cause symptomatic hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Monitor blood pressure after initiation and titrate doses accordingly

contraindications.reason: Accelerate CKD progression and cause fluid retention; eGFR 4.9 mL/min/1.73 m²
eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – high risk of lactic acidosis
Increases risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury; NG203 contraindicates dual RAAS blockade
High risk of contrast‑induced nephropathy with eGFR <30
contraindications.alternative: Use prophylactic hydration and low‑osmolar contrast if imaging unavoidable

treatment_summary: Start low‑dose ramipril and atorvastatin as first‑line therapy for CKD progression and cardiovascular risk. Add amlodipine only if blood pressure remains uncontrolled after ACE‑I titration. Address CKD‑related anemia with epoetin alfa after confirming iron status, and correct vitamin D deficiency with calcifediol. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, liver enzymes, haemoglobin, iron studies, and bone‑mineral parameters per NG203, and avoid contraindicated agents such as NSAIDs, metformin, and dual RAAS blockade.
